SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business

property noun

what someone owns

also possessions, belongings, assets, personal property, fortune

classical

Cic. Sest. 54: bona mea dīripiēbantur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Caecin. 38: bona, fortūnās, possessiōnēs omnium (Lewis & Short)

bona, bonōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

goods, property, all one owns

Almost always the whole of one’s possessions (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Rēs autem familiāris quaerī dēbet iīs rēbus, ā quibus abest turpitūdō, cōnservārī autem dīligentiā et parsimōniā, eīsdem etiam rēbus augērī.

    Property should be acquired by means that have nothing shameful about them, kept by care and thrift, and increased by the same.Cic. Off. 2.87

Other words

  • rēs familiāris — one’s property, the family’s means

    noun and adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.87: rēs autem familiāris quaerī dēbet iīs rēbus, ā quibus abest turpitūdō

  • fortūnae, fortūnārum f. pl. — one’s fortune, possessions

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 19: multī rem ac fortūnās āmittere

See also own, property, money.

SourcesLewis & Short: bonum · Lewis & Short: familiaris · Lewis & Short: fortuna

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
